speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Prime Minister what is the scope of guidance or control on the choice of monetary regime or on the total level of reserves held, that the Government is able to convey to or exercise on MAS as an independent central bank.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have addressed questions on the Official Foreign Reserves (OFRs) in this House several times, most recently during the Second Reading Speech on the MAS (Amendment) Bill on 11 January 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These covered the purpose of maintaining OFR, how it is accumulated, how it is invested and how much of it is needed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am just wondering if I could just clarify.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, my interpretation of what was just shared is that MAS actually does maintain quite a bit of discretion in how it operationalises the various scopes, but that the Government is able to make broad suggestions on just how it goes about operationalising these principles.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And if that is the case, would the Minister of State be able to share if this is also the general principle that the Government adheres to for all other independent bodies, such as the Chief Valuer?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And the structure of the MAS and, indeed, how MAS conducts its exchange rate monetary policy is not new.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, it has been something that is a long-stated policy of the MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Many advanced countries have opted for statutory central bank independence, but this has not really fully insulated monetary policy from political interference.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If we take a step back and look at over five decades of MAS' history – MAS has built its credibility as a central bank, as a financial supervisor as well as a partner with industry, by learning from the best.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Particularly in  MAS' earlier years, but also where appropriate, doing things in our own way.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And that is why the way that we do things are different.
